collections.label: Introduction to Science
collections.learningIntention: Students will understand that key science terms help scientists describe investigations, evidence, data and explanations clearly.
collections.successCriteria: Students can identify introductory science vocabulary from letter patterns, clues and definitions, then explain the meaning of each term.

items.clue: A testable prediction about what might happen in an investigation.
items.definition: A hypothesis is a testable prediction that links an independent variable to a dependent variable.

items.clue: Information collected using your senses or scientific instruments.
items.definition: An observation is information gathered by looking, listening, measuring, smelling or using scientific tools.

items.clue: A practical test used to investigate a question or claim.
items.definition: An experiment is a planned test used to collect evidence about a scientific question.

items.clue: A statement about what you think will happen.
items.definition: A prediction states what is expected to happen, often based on prior knowledge or a scientific idea.

items.clue: A factor that can change in an investigation.
items.definition: A variable is something that can change or be changed in an investigation.

items.clue: The variable that is deliberately changed in a fair test.
items.definition: The independent variable is the factor deliberately changed to see what effect it has.

items.clue: The variable that is measured or observed in a fair test.
items.definition: The dependent variable is the factor measured to see how it responds to the independent variable.

items.clue: A factor kept the same to make an investigation fair.
items.definition: A controlled variable is kept the same so the test focuses on the effect of the independent variable.

items.clue: A structured process for asking questions, testing ideas and using evidence.
items.definition: The scientific method is a process scientists use to investigate questions and develop evidence-based explanations.

items.clue: A wide container used to hold, mix or heat liquids.
items.definition: A beaker is a laboratory container used for holding, mixing and sometimes heating liquids.

items.clue: Equipment used to measure the volume of a liquid more accurately than a beaker.
items.definition: A measuring cylinder is used to measure liquid volume in millilitres.

items.clue: A tool used to measure temperature.
items.definition: A thermometer measures temperature, usually in degrees Celsius in Australian classrooms.

items.clue: An instrument used to view very small objects.
items.definition: A microscope magnifies small objects, such as cells, so they can be seen more clearly.

items.clue: A gas burner used to heat materials in the laboratory.
items.definition: A Bunsen burner is a laboratory burner used to heat substances safely when used correctly.

items.clue: A small glass tube used to hold small amounts of substances.
items.definition: A test tube is used to hold, mix or heat small amounts of chemicals.

items.clue: Equipment used to hold clamps and support apparatus during experiments.
items.definition: A retort stand supports equipment such as clamps, burettes, funnels or test tubes during practical work.

items.clue: Information collected during an investigation.
items.definition: Data is information collected through observations, measurements or research.

items.clue: Data or observations used to support a scientific explanation.
items.definition: Evidence is information used to support or challenge a claim or explanation.

items.clue: How close a measurement is to the true or accepted value.
items.definition: Accuracy describes how close a measurement is to the correct or accepted value.

items.clue: How consistent results are when an investigation is repeated.
items.definition: Reliability describes whether repeated trials produce consistent results.

items.clue: How well an investigation tests what it is supposed to test.
items.definition: Validity describes whether an investigation is fair and actually tests the intended question.

items.clue: A general pattern shown in results.
items.definition: A trend is a pattern or relationship shown by data.

items.clue: A result that does not fit the general pattern.
items.definition: An outlier is a value that is noticeably different from the rest of the data.

items.clue: Safety equipment used to protect your eyes.
items.definition: Goggles protect the eyes from splashes, fragments and other laboratory hazards.

items.clue: Something that could cause harm.
items.definition: A hazard is anything that has the potential to cause harm.

items.clue: The chance that a hazard will cause harm.
items.definition: Risk is the likelihood that a hazard will cause harm, combined with how serious the harm could be.

items.clue: A document that gives safety information about a chemical.
items.definition: A safety data sheet provides information about chemical hazards, safe handling, storage and emergency actions.

items.clue: When a substance is accidentally dropped or spread where it should not be.
items.definition: A spill is an accidental release of a substance and should be reported to the teacher immediately.

items.clue: When unwanted substances or organisms get into a sample.
items.definition: Contamination occurs when unwanted material gets into a sample, experiment or environment.
